title: Black Sea Grain Initiative is signed in Istanbul
body:
The Black Sea Grain Initiative was signed in Istanbul on 22 July 2022 at Dolmabahce Palace. Present at the ceremony were UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Turkish Defence Minister Hulusi Akar, together with Ukrainian Infrastructure Minister Oleksandr Kubrakov and Russian Defence Minister Sergei Shoigu. The arrangement allowed grain, other foodstuffs and fertilizer to be exported from Ukrainian ports during the war, at a time of concern about global food prices.

Three Ukrainian ports were covered: Odesa, Chornomorsk and Yuzhny/Pivdennyi. A Joint Coordination Centre, hosted in Istanbul, monitored implementation. It included representatives of Russia, Turkey, Ukraine and the United Nations, with the UN serving as its secretariat. Joint inspection teams checked ships heading to and from Ukrainian ports.

The initiative was linked to separate efforts to bring Russian food and fertilizer to global markets, and the UN set up a task force on Russian exports led by Rebeca Grynspan of UNCTAD. The initiative ran for three terms. The third term expired on 17 July 2023, and the initiative was not renewed. The UN page itself gives conflicting dates for the ceremony, 22 July in a photo caption and 27 July in the main text; 22 July is the date used in other UN material.
